decisions.statement: A package reached and not named is one half of the rule.
A dependency named and not reached is the other half.
One reading of the manifests and the reaches answers both halves.
A dependency is a name the manifest states under any dependency field of its own.
A dependency judged for going unreached is stated under `dependencies` or `devDependencies`.
A reach in code is read from the parse rather than from the text.
A stylesheet names a module by an `@import` or by a `url()`.
A reach in a stylesheet is found by scanning rather than by a parse.
A url naming a scheme or a fragment reaches no package.
A stylesheet's reach credits a dependency rather than refusing the stylesheet.
A specifier spelt inside a string a body has reaches nothing.
A specifier naming a path reaches no package.
A specifier naming a protocol reaches no package.
A bare specifier naming a builtin of the runtime reaches no package.
The builtins are asked of the runtime rather than listed here.
A reach at a package the akasha folder itself has is let through.
The name the root's own manifest states is a package the akasha folder has.
The root is reached without any manifest naming the root.
A dependency naming a package the akasha folder itself has is let through.
A file is judged against the innermost package whose folder has that file.
A file standing under no package is passed over.
The files a package has are the files there are as the change leaves them.
A change carrying no manifest is judged without the files being listed.
A package reached is named by its own name or by the `@types` package standing for that package.
Whether a reach is erased at compile time is not read here.
A dependency a package states as a peer of its own is reached by the installer of that package.
A dependency another dependency states as a peer is reached by that other dependency.
A dependency a script names as a command is reached by that script.
`typescript` is reached by a `tsconfig.json` standing in the package's folder.
`@types/bun` is reached by a `bun:` specifier.
`@types/node` is reached by a `node:` specifier.
An `@types` package is reached by the package the `@types` package stands for.
A dependency a package's page names under `tool-reached` is reached by a tool.
A tool taking a dependency out of the manifest leaves no import for this check to read.
The list is read off the page whose folder has the manifest.
The page is read as the change leaves the page.
A page naming nothing under `tool-reached` credits nothing by that list.
A file reaching a package its manifest does not name is refused by its own path.
A dependency reached by nothing is refused at its manifest's path.
A dependency reached by nothing is judged where the change has its manifest.
A manifest that is absent or will not parse leaves its package unjudged.
An index naming no package judges clean.

definition: the check judging a package's dependencies and the packages its own code reaches to be one set
